items.summary: Anthropic has released an open-source tool called sandbox-runtime, designed to provide OS-level isolation for AI agents without using containers. The tool restricts file access and network connections for processes, including scripts and subprocesses. It operates on macOS using Seatbelt and on Linux using bubblewrap, with Windows support currently in alpha. Anthropic reports that using this sandbox reduced permission prompts by 84% in internal Claude Code usage. The tool allows developers to define allowlists for domains and file paths to balance security with agent functionality.
items.title: Anthropic Releases Open-Source OS-Level Sandbox for AI Agents

items.summary: Jason Carney, former CTO of Luminar, compares the current AI infrastructure race to the autonomous vehicle sector of 2022. He notes that technology companies like Tesla and Waymo drove past traditional automakers. Similarly, AI firms are bypassing traditional power and telecom providers to build their own optical networking infrastructure, effectively becoming infrastructure companies themselves.
items.title: Luminar Cofounder Compares AI Infrastructure Shift to Autonomous Vehicle History

items.summary: Following the public disclosure of PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, millions of exploitation attempts occurred within hours, aided by AI tools that simplified the process for attackers. While no successful breaches have been confirmed, researchers note that AI has accelerated the analysis of flaws known for years. Experts suggest that while AI magnifies existing risks, human expertise remains essential for discovery, and the scope of such attacks may be limited compared to other software.
items.title: AI Tools Accelerate Exploitation of Long-Standing PHP Vulnerabilities

items.summary: This tutorial demonstrates building a stateful engineering copilot using Letta. It covers creating inspectable core memory blocks, archival vector memory for semantic retrieval, custom tools for risk estimation, and shared state for multi-agent collaboration. The guide also details streaming execution traces and exporting agent workflows for portability.
items.title: Tutorial Demonstrates Stateful Agentic Engineering Copilots with Letta

items.summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has proposed a draft regulation requiring cyan-colored lights on vehicles operating autonomously to help emergency responders identify driverless cars. This suggestion follows a similar proposal by Mercedes and a draft standard from China, which uses turquoise and takes effect in 2028. The NHTSA's rule is optional but aims to standardize identification, addressing safety concerns regarding emergency response. The proposal also updates Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards to accommodate autonomous vehicle designs, such as removing turn signal requirements for cars without steering wheels. The draft will be open for public comment for 30 days.
items.title: NHTSA Proposes Cyan Lights for Autonomous Vehicles

items.summary: A survey of 2,000 Black and Latino registered voters in swing states reveals that while many support climate policy, rising costs dominate their election priorities. Only 9 percent ranked climate change among their top three voting issues, compared to 74 percent for the cost of living. Respondents expressed skepticism that environmental protections would lower bills or improve air and water quality without immediate economic relief. Advocates argue that voters connect climate issues to tangible concerns like electricity costs and pollution, rather than abstract concepts. Despite this, most still want candidates to prioritize climate change, suggesting a desire for solutions that address both affordability and environmental health.
items.title: Black Voters Prioritize Cost of Living Over Climate Action

items.summary: India's solar and energy storage industry expanded significantly at the Renewable Energy India Expo 2026, attracting over 54,000 visitors and 1,000 exhibitors. Analysts estimate the country now possesses more than 200 GW of annual module capacity, far exceeding the expected 50-60 GW demand through 2030. This surplus predicts a market shakeout beginning in 2027, where manufacturers lacking local cell production will struggle. While most focus on TOPCon technology, Reliance Industries is building a 20 GW heterojunction supply chain. Several companies plan to produce wafers locally by 2028 to meet domestic content requirements, signaling a shift toward vertical integration despite short-term price pressures.
items.title: India's Solar Industry Faces Capacity Shakeout Amid Growth

items.summary: EGO Commercial introduced a new line of zero-turn mowers, a leaf blower, and a trimmer at the EQUIP Expo. The equipment features a 56V PGX battery system and includes models with up to 44 gas-equivalent horsepower and speeds reaching 12 mph. EGO highlighted an expanded battery ecosystem and a connected platform to help landscapers manage energy needs. Tim Baker, vice president of product at Chervon, stated the focus is on delivering performance to maximize productivity. The lineup also features a 3200W PGX Hub offering 30 kWh of charging capacity.
items.title: EGO Commercial Unveils New Electric Landscaping Equipment Line

items.summary: New research indicates that while Beijing's overall air quality has improved due to policies introduced around 2008, concentrations of sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) are accelerating. This potent greenhouse gas, 24,300 times more effective than carbon dioxide, is driven by surging electricity demand and the rapid expansion of semiconductor manufacturing linked to the AI boom. Although the electric power sector accounts for about 70 percent of global SF6 emissions, semiconductor manufacturing has become the primary local source in Beijing. The study, published in Environmental Science & Technology, highlights these sectors as critical targets for emission control.
items.title: SF6 Emissions Surge in Beijing Amid AI and Semiconductor Growth

items.summary: Mozambique has selected the UAE-based Jampur Group to manage and modernize the Beluluane Solar Panel Factory in Maputo province. This agreement follows a 2024 restructuring initiative by FUNAE aimed at improving efficiency. The factory, inaugurated in 2013 with $13 million investment, suspended production in 2022 due to outdated technology and competition from cheaper imports. Provincial governor Manuel Tule emphasized recruiting local youth while acknowledging skill gaps.
items.title: Mozambique Selects UAE Firm to Revive Struggling Solar Factory

items.summary: Google announced a major update for the Fitbit Air, expanding automatic workout detection to over 100 activities and introducing the Health Guardian feature. This new tool tracks trends in blood pressure and insulin resistance for Google Health Premium subscribers, aiming to provide deeper health insights alongside fitness data.
items.title: Google Updates Fitbit Air with Enhanced Health Tracking Features

items.summary: Oppo launched the Pad Mini in India at ₹94,999, featuring an 8.8-inch OLED display, 8000mAh battery, and AI tools. The device aims to compete with the upcoming Apple iPad Mini 8, though the latter's specifications remain unconfirmed.
items.title: Oppo Launches Pad Mini to Challenge Apple in India

items.summary: Skydance employees anticipate a restructuring following the $110bn merger of Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery. CEO David Ellison aims to reduce an $80bn debt load and generate $6bn in savings within three years, though management warns of difficult workforce decisions. Concerns persist regarding potential job cuts and the political influence of Ellison and investor Elon Musk on editorial independence. While Ellison pledged to release 30 major films annually until 2031, analysts question the sustainability of this strategy. The new entity faces challenges balancing debt reduction, content investment, and maintaining journalistic integrity across its diverse portfolio of studios and news outlets.
items.title: Skydance Employees Face Uncertainty Amid Megamerger Restructure Plans

items.summary: Charlotte Riley, who organises the Christmas Kindness Appeal Jersey, reports a rise in families seeking help for Christmas presents. Riley, who started the initiative in 2024, noted an unexpected increase in demand driven by unemployment, ill health, and high living costs. While noting that more people are also offering to help, she emphasises the growing need for support among families with children up to 18 years old.
items.title: Rising Demand for Christmas Help Grows in Jersey

items.summary: A management consultant is gaining viral attention after sharing anonymous direct messages sent by bosses to employees. The messages, described as cringe-worthy, include inappropriate content sent on occasions such as a wedding day. The consultant started sharing these messages to expose the behavior.
items.title: Management Consultant Goes Viral for Exposing Cringe-Worthy Boss DMs

items.summary: Leading UK restaurateurs are opening branches in Gulf states like Dubai and Abu Dhabi, citing a 'tax tsunami' in the UK and better work ethics abroad. James Robson, co-owner of Fallow, noted that the UK's 20% hospitality VAT is among the highest in Europe, compared to around 12% in Europe and 10% in Italy. While some restaurants like Dinner by Heston have struggled due to regional conflicts, others continue to expand. However, human rights experts warn of poor worker protections and exploitation in the Gulf, where migrant workers are often bound by sponsorship systems. Despite this, chefs argue that the UK lacks a risk-reward balance for business growth.
items.title: Top UK Chefs Open Gulf Outposts Amid Tax Concerns

items.summary: At the Financial Street Forum 2026, Simon Richards of BNY Investments and Laszlo Krisar discussed the concept of smart spending. They explored how careful financial planning, from individual pensions to global economics, contributes to long-term resilience. The dialogue highlighted mindful spending as a potential strategy for future stability in an inclusive world economy.
items.title: Global Leaders Discuss Smart Spending Trends at Financial Forum

items.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi stated that China and the United States share the responsibility to jointly develop and govern artificial intelligence. Speaking in Xiongan on October 23, 2026, he emphasized the need to guard against risks while promoting cooperation to establish global rules. Wang noted that AI should remain under human control and benefit people, urging inclusive development for common prosperity and security.
items.title: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi Calls for China-US AI Cooperation

items.summary: French police arrested more than 130 people and deployed 70,000 security forces as nationwide protests against the cost of living began on Saturday. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez stated there were no early signs of the street violence seen the previous weekend, though police confiscated weapons and fired tear gas in Lyon. While the government banned non-union-led demonstrations, organizers and unions criticized the move as an attack on protest rights. Tensions remain high ahead of a presidential election, with Marine Le Pen's party launching a campaign and anti-fascist groups marching against her.
items.title: French Police Arrest 130 Protesters Amid Cost of Living Demonstrations

items.summary: Paula Moltzan secured her first career World Cup victory in giant slalom at Soelden, Austria, on October 24. At 32, she beat Mikaela Shiffrin by 0.01 seconds after the American skier fell from a first-leg lead. Moltzan, skiing on Van Deer skis, finished fifth after the first run to claim the win. This result marks her 11th podium finish.
items.title: Paula Moltzan Wins First World Cup at Soelden

items.summary: The Metropolitan Police confirmed they shared allegations of child sexual abuse involving Thomas Markle Sr with the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex in January 2019. The force stated the information was not passed to other law enforcement agencies. Meghan Markle expressed distress over the claims, which her father denied as lies. The police are reviewing their handling of the matter and considering a referral to the Independent Office for Police Conduct. Markle later clarified the year was 2019, not 2018 as initially stated.
items.title: Met Police Confirm Sharing Abuse Allegations With Meghan Markle

items.summary: The Metropolitan Police confirmed it received a letter containing claims against Meghan Markle's father in January 2019. A spokesperson stated the police did not share the letter with other agencies. This confirmation comes amid separate allegations that child sexual abuse material was found at Thomas Markle's former home in the Philippines.
items.title: Met Police Confirms Receipt of Letter Regarding Meghan Markle's Father

items.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un visited China to inaugurate the New Yalu River Bridge, aiming to expand cooperation. He met Chinese official Wang Huning and toured a car factory. The visit, timed before a Korean War anniversary, underscores strengthened ties with Beijing as relations with Seoul deteriorate. Kim expressed readiness to deliver tangible benefits through practical cooperation.
items.title: Kim Jong-un Inaugurates New Bridge to China Amid Diplomatic Push

items.summary: Ukraine states that Starlink satellite internet has returned to normal operating speeds following a period of throttling that hindered military operations. The restrictions emerged after Donald Trump announced a deal to purchase Russian diesel, which pressured Kyiv to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries. Trump indicated he would resolve any persistent issues if they continued.
items.title: Ukraine Reports Starlink Service Restoration After Military Disruptions

items.summary: Opposition supporters and students in Tirana, Albania, mobilized on Saturday, burning symbolic pillows outside Prime Minister Edi Rama's office before marching toward the Ministry of Education. Police deployed water cannons and riot units as demonstrators hurled rocks at the building and officers. Rama acknowledged public discontent but warned that the state's response to violence would be prolonged and persistent.
items.title: Protesters Burn Pillows Outside Albanian Prime Minister's Office Amid Rising Tensions

items.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz accused Russia of seeking to destabilize Germany, citing cyberattacks, sabotage, and threats to critical infrastructure as endangering European security. Merz, speaking at a convention in Munich, stated that Russia's war against Ukraine has shaken the European peace order and that the threat extends beyond Ukraine. Federal Intelligence Service President Martin Jaeger previously warned that Germany faces a direct threat of violent conflict with Russia, referencing an attempted drone strike on a Ukrainian cargo plane in August.
items.title: German Chancellor Merz Accuses Russia of Seeking to Destabilize Germany Amid Growing Security Threats

items.summary: French police and gendarmes deployed Centaure armoured vehicles in Paris and Marseille on Saturday, 24 October, as authorities prepared for demonstrations over the rising cost of living. In Paris, an armoured vehicle was stationed behind the National Assembly, while in Marseille, security forces patrolled alongside armoured vehicles and a water cannon. The deployment follows concerns about potential violence, including clashes, looting, and arson in several French cities the previous weekend.
items.title: French Police Deploy Armoured Vehicles in Paris and Marseille Ahead of Protests

items.summary: Belen Sanz Luque, UN Women's regional director for Europe and Central Asia, urged the inclusion of women in peacebuilding efforts for Gaza and Sudan. Drawing on Colombia's peace process with FARC, she emphasized that women's leadership is critical for sustainable peace. Sanz noted that while international commitments exist, only 5% of peace agreements in 2025 had women as negotiators. She highlighted that agreements are 35% more likely to be implemented successfully when women participate. Sanz stressed the need for mechanisms to enforce these commitments rather than relying on political goodwill.
items.title: UN Women Official Calls for Women's Inclusion in Gaza Peacebuilding

items.summary: NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell stated that the league plans to host a regular-season game in Tokyo in either 2027 or 2028. Goodell, speaking on Friday, emphasized that Tokyo is a priority market and highlighted the success of previous international trips to Melbourne, Rio, and Madrid as evidence of the NFL's expanding global reach and ability to manage travel logistics.
items.title: NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell Targets Tokyo for 2027 or 2028

items.summary: Ukraine's defence minister stated that the nation now has a stable Starlink connection following days of restricted connectivity affecting military operations. Kyiv accused US President Donald Trump of instructing Elon Musk to impose speed limits, a claim Trump denied. Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara confirmed speeds exceeding 400km/h are now possible, indicating full capability restoration. Zelensky also addressed threats regarding intelligence sharing.
items.title: Ukraine reports stable Starlink connection after connectivity limits

items.summary: Gunmen opened fire at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, Jordan, during a funeral, killing seven people and wounding 40 others, authorities said. The attack occurred on Friday, with footage showing three men firing weapons before fleeing. Jordan declared three days of national mourning. King Abdullah II condemned the act, while regional leaders offered condolences. Investigations are underway.
items.title: Gunmen Kill 7 and Wound 40 at Jordan Church Funeral

items.summary: A 36-year-old British woman died after attempting to rescue her two sons who were swept away by a strong current while snorkelling in the Bahamas. The Royal Bahamas Police Force stated that foul play is not suspected and an autopsy is pending. The Foreign Office expressed condolences and confirmed support for the family.
items.title: British Woman Dies Attempting to Rescue Sons in Bahamas

items.summary: Senshu Ikeda and Shiga Bank are discussing a merger to form the largest regional banking group in the Kansai region, according to unnamed sources. An announcement is expected next week, though neither bank has finalized the deal. The combined entity would hold ¥14.6 trillion in assets, surpassing Kyoto Financial Group Inc.
items.title: Senshu Ikeda and Shiga Bank Plan Regional Merger

items.summary: A final campaign push is underway in Brazil ahead of the Sunday presidential runoff between incumbent Luis Ignácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. Bolsonaro finished first in the initial round with 47 percent of the vote compared to Lula's 45 percent. Polls indicate the race remains tight. Lula seeks a fourth non-consecutive term, while Bolsonaro aims to succeed his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is currently imprisoned. The election outcome will influence Brazil's relations with the United States, where President Trump supports the Bolsonaro family, and determine leadership of South America's largest economy for the next four years.
items.title: Brazilian Candidates Push Ahead of Presidential Runoff

items.summary: A scuffle erupted in the Albanian parliament as opposition members blocked the podium and clashed with lawmakers over ongoing student demonstrations in the capital. Footage captured overturned chairs and confrontations inside the assembly, while protesters outside pulled down security barriers. Lawmakers displayed photos of injured students to express solidarity, highlighting the escalation of tensions from the streets into political institutions.
items.title: Albanian MPs Clash Over Student Protests in Parliament

items.summary: Poland is integrating the restoration of the Białowieża Forest into its border defense strategy, a concept known as 'warwilding.' Scientists and military officials propose that restoring wetlands and forests creates a natural barrier against heavy vehicles. While the Ministry of Defence has embraced this idea, implementation remains slow. Conservationists note that decades of drainage and road construction have degraded the ecosystem. Despite diverting over $120 million in EU funds, progress is hindered by legislative procedures and the need for drastic action to stop water outflow and road widening. The alliance between generals and conservationists aims to protect the UNESCO site while enhancing national security.
items.title: Poland Integrates Forest Restoration into Border Defense Strategy

items.summary: Farmers in rural Iowa are grappling with rising costs for fuel, insurance, and repairs, creating significant anxiety despite the approaching harvest. While some, like Chip Hoffman, blame tariffs and the war with Iran for squeezing profit margins, others note that high input costs persist under both Democratic and Republican administrations. Despite these economic struggles, many farmers remain skeptical about the impact of the upcoming midterm elections on their daily lives. However, political figures like Senate candidate Josh Turek and Governor candidate Rob Sand argue that the current political climate is decimating agricultural markets and that a change in leadership is necessary to address tariff issues. Data indicates that 64% of registered voters in Iowa live in rural communities, highlighting the potential influence of this demographic in the swing state.
items.title: Iowa Farmers Face Economic Hardship Amid Political Uncertainty

items.summary: Aggressive redistricting efforts by Democrats and Republicans aim to secure additional congressional seats in the upcoming U.S. midterm elections. While Republicans in Texas seek five new seats, California's Proposition 50 targets five for Democrats. Twelve states have redrawn maps ahead of schedule, though outcomes remain uncertain due to reliance on outdated polls.
items.title: Partisan Redistricting Efforts Shift Seats in U.S. Midterms

items.summary: Alexander Embiricos, co-founder of the remote collaboration platform Multi, joined OpenAI following the company's acquisition of his startup in June 2024. Embiricos initially led Multi's team before transitioning to product roles at OpenAI, first on the Codex team and later as product lead for the Dots AI agent. Multi ceased operations in July 2024 as part of the deal.
items.title: Alexander Embiricos Joins OpenAI After Building Multi

items.summary: President Droupadi Murmu's two-day visit to Odisha has been postponed to November 4-5 due to cyclone threats. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to inaugurate the RBI's Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar on Sunday. Elaborate security arrangements, including 70 platoons of personnel, are in place for the Prime Minister's visit.
items.title: President Murmu's Odisha Visit Postponed Due to Cyclone Threat

items.summary: Jio Platforms is expected to rank among India's three largest listed companies with an implied valuation of ₹10.3 lakh crore. Its IPO closed with 22.19 times subscription, attracting ₹7.4 lakh crore in demand despite market volatility. The listing could also make Reliance Group India's largest listed business group by aggregate market capitalisation.
items.title: Jio Platforms Expected to Rank Among India's Top Three Firms After Listing

items.summary: Reports indicate that various Android devices, including the Google Pixel 8 Pro and Vivo X300 Ultra, currently display a Google Play system update date of January 1, 2027. Experts attribute this to a labeling error rather than an actual future software release. The issue affects devices running Android 12 and newer. Users are advised not to assume their devices have received future security patches or features based on this display.
items.title: Android phones display incorrect 2027 update date due to labeling error

items.summary: US President Donald Trump claimed at a Florida rally that a threat to impose 250% tariffs on India and Pakistan prevented a full-scale war in May 2025. He stated the nations halted hostilities after his intervention, asserting the United Nations played no role. India has rejected this assertion, maintaining the ceasefire was reached directly between the two countries without third-party mediation. The conflict followed India's Operation Sindoor targeting terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir after an April 2025 attack in Pahalgam.
items.title: Trump Claims Tariff Threats Stopped India-Pakistan War

items.summary: Indian Railways has extended its Optional Travel Insurance Scheme (OTIS) to passengers booking reserved tickets through Passenger Reservation System counters starting October 27, complying with Supreme Court directions. Under the scheme, passengers can opt for insurance by paying a premium of 45 paise per passenger, offering coverage of up to ₹10 lakh in case of death or permanent total disability arising from a railway accident or untoward incident.
items.title: Indian Railways Extends Travel Insurance Scheme to Reserved Ticket Bookers

items.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party claims Shiv Sena MP Sanjay Raut orchestrated a fake audio clip alleging a Rs 500 crore bribe to Maratha activist Manoj Jarange. BJP spokesperson Navnath Ban alleges the clip was generated using artificial intelligence to create a rift among ruling alliance partners. Raut denies the conspiracy, blaming internal BJP rivalry for the leak. Jarange released the audio, alleging a conspiracy to silence him and weaken the reservation movement. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis ordered a forensic examination of the clip amid the allegations.
items.title: BJP and Shiv Sena Clash Over Alleged Fake Audio Clip

items.summary: Security forces arrested 17 Kuki militants in Manipur's Kangpokpi district during an operation at Mt Sinai Camp. Police stated the arrested individuals' identities did not match registered cadres under the Suspension of Operation agreement. Authorities recovered 24 automatic weapons and other arms. The Manipur Home Minister noted the SoO pact has expired, and new recruitment is now illegal.
items.title: 17 Kuki Militants Arrested in Manipur Over Identity Mismatch

items.summary: The Supreme Court halted Andhra Pradesh local body polls following violence during nominations. The ruling Telugu Desam Party and opposition Yuvajana Sramika Rythu Congress Party exchanged accusations regarding obstruction and assaults. Separately, tensions rose at Jamia Millia Islamia after Congress MPs entered the campus, prompting the registrar to accuse them of provoking students on hunger strike. The administration moved classes online while police lodged complaints against the leaders.
items.title: Supreme Court Halts Andhra Polls Amid Political Violence and Campus Tensions

items.summary: Erin and Chris Amerman purchased a 210-acre farm near Gainesville, Florida, in 2015 and founded Critter Creek Farm Sanctuary in 2016. Starting with three rescued cows, the non-profit expanded to 420 acres across three properties by acquiring Critter Hills in 2019. Today, the sanctuary houses more than 180 cows, along with donkeys, pigs, horses, and other species. The Amermans state their mission is to foster compassion through science-based rescue and conservation, hosting monthly tours and public events to connect visitors with the animals.
items.title: Amermans Grow Florida Sanctuary from Three Cows to 180 Animals

items.summary: Selena Gomez sold her Encino, California mansion for $5.399 million on September 8, 2026. The property, previously owned by Tom Petty, had been purchased by Gomez for $4.895 million in 2020. The sale price was approximately $1.1 million below the original listing price of $6.5 million. Gomez recently acquired a larger Beverly Hills estate with her husband, Benny Blanco.
items.title: Selena Gomez Sells Former Tom Petty Home for $5.399 Million

items.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party accused the Congress party of undermining constitutional institutions and seeking foreign support for recent protests. Simultaneously, Jamia Millia Islamia Registrar Mahtab Alam Rizvi accused Congress MPs of entering the campus and provoking students on hunger strike. The administration moved classes online due to security concerns, while Ravinder Raina condemned Farooq Abdullah's remarks on Kashmir as sedition.
items.title: BJP Accuses Congress of Undermining Constitution Amid Campus Tensions

items.summary: Hansgrohe India aims to achieve double-digit growth in the Hyderabad-Telangana region over the next two years by expanding its retail network from 17 to 22 stores. The company hosted a Developer Dialogue with over 50 stakeholders to address evolving expectations in the luxury residential market. Abdulkader Bengali, Managing Director, emphasized the region's growing aspirations for quality and thoughtfully designed homes as a key driver for this expansion.
items.title: Hansgrohe India Targets Double-Digit Growth in Hyderabad-Telangana

items.summary: The Centre created 11 crore unique farmer IDs under the AgriStack framework five months before the March 2027 deadline. Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan stated this milestone was achieved under the Digital Agriculture Mission. The initiative aims to provide farmers with a unique digital identity to access government schemes and credit efficiently. Officials noted that 26 per cent of registered farmers are women.
items.title: Centre issues 11 crore farmer IDs under AgriStack ahead of schedule

items.summary: The National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) has released a 20-hour introductory module on artificial intelligence and computational thinking for students in Classes 9 to 12. Developed by faculty from IIT Madras, IIT Jodhpur, and NCERT, the activity-based curriculum aligns with the National Education Policy 2020. It covers five units focusing on AI systems, machine learning, misinformation, data privacy under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023, and responsible tool usage. The module emphasizes practical learning over memorization, encouraging students to verify information and maintain human judgment. School principals from the CBSE have welcomed the initiative as a significant step toward preparing students for a technology-driven future.
items.title: NCERT Launches 20-Hour AI Module for Classes 9 to 12

items.summary: Castrol India's net profit fell 22.6% to ₹176.37 crore in Q3 2026 due to surging raw-material costs and adverse currency movements. Revenue rose 27.3% to ₹1,734.72 crore, but EBITDA declined 18.8%. The results coincide with BP's proposed sale of a 65% stake in Castrol's global business to Stonepeak, valued at $10 billion, which would give Stonepeak indirect control of Castrol India.
items.title: Castrol India Profit Falls Amid Rising Costs and Ownership Change

items.summary: The Central Administrative Tribunal refused to quash disciplinary proceedings against IPS officer Aditya Kumar, accused of conspiring to impersonate a former Chief Justice. While the tribunal rejected Kumar's claims of malicious intent, it directed the state government to conclude the inquiry within six months. Separately, the Bihar Home Department closed proceedings related to Kumar's tenure as Gaya SSP, but this does not invalidate the ongoing impersonation case.
items.title: CAT Upholds Disciplinary Proceedings Against IPS Officer Aditya Kumar

items.summary: A SIDBI survey indicates MSME confidence rebounded in the July-September quarter of FY27, with the index rising to 60.4. While 49% of enterprises reported improved conditions, margin pressures persist. Trading firms lag behind manufacturing and services in both confidence and sales sentiment. Access to working capital remains a key challenge for the sector.
items.title: MSME Confidence Rebounds Amid Margin Pressures

items.summary: Jamia Millia Islamia shifted classes online following student protests demanding union elections. Students alleged administration attacks on hunger strikers, while the university cited safety concerns. Officials formed a committee to draft a constitution by December 20, but students view this as a delaying tactic and plan to continue their hunger strike until election notifications are released.
items.title: Jamia Millia Islamia shifts classes online amid student union election protests

items.summary: The Tamil Nadu government reduced VAT on aviation turbine fuel to 16% at Chennai and 1% elsewhere, effective until October 31, 2027. Civil Aviation Minister K Ram Mohan Naidu welcomed the move as essential for affordable air travel. The state aims to lower airline costs and expand regional routes amid rising global fuel prices and currency pressures.
items.title: Tamil Nadu Cuts Aviation Fuel VAT to Boost Connectivity

items.summary: The Almora Literature Festival (ALF) was established to celebrate the town's underexplored cultural and intellectual heritage, distinguishing it from typical colonial hill stations. Organized by Vasudha Pant, the event takes place at the historic Malla Mahal from October 30 to November 1. The festival aims to bring folk stories and local traditions to the forefront, recognizing figures like Pandit Uday Shankar and Gaura Pant who shaped the region's literary landscape. By hosting the event at a site built in 1588, ALF seeks to preserve Kumauni history and create a genuine platform for voices often overshadowed by tourism.
items.title: Almora Launches Literature Festival to Celebrate Heritage

items.summary: The UK government has launched the 'Be Ready' campaign, advising households to store three days' worth of food, water, and cash. Prime Minister Andy Burnham urged citizens to take sensible precautions rather than panic buy, citing severe weather, cyberattacks, and threats from hostile states as potential disruptors of essential services. Specific recommendations include keeping nine litres of water per person and non-perishable food. The advice follows recent storms that left homes without power and a major cybersecurity incident involving PHP vulnerabilities. Defence Secretary Wes Streeting warned that cyber incidents could increase due to the AI boom, while the National Audit Office noted growing threats to the food supply chain.
items.title: UK Government Urges Citizens to Stockpile Emergency Supplies Amid Rising Threats

items.summary: Delhi police are investigating the death of an 18-year-old Class 12 student found burnt behind a school guard room in Krishna Nagar. Fire officer Anoop Singh stated a child had set a fire inside the school. While some media reports suggest suicide, authorities are examining circumstances and have recovered materials and the student's bag. The body was sent for a post-mortem.
items.title: Delhi Police Investigate Burnt Class 12 Student Found Behind School Guard Room

items.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay announced a reduction in aviation fuel tax from 29 percent to 16 percent at Chennai airport and 1 percent at other state airports. The Union Civil Aviation Minister welcomed the move as a step for the aviation sector. While the decision highlights cooperation between the state and Centre, the article notes it does not confirm a shift in the TVK government's political alignment.
items.title: Tamil Nadu cuts aviation fuel tax, drawing Centre praise

items.summary: A report from Groww notes that small and mid-cap funds attracted Rs 16,873 crore in September, representing 44% of equity inflows. Despite this, valuations remain stretched compared to large caps, which saw outflows. The report suggests investors should assess valuations alongside flows rather than relying solely on inflows as a signal of opportunity.
items.title: Smallcap Mutual Funds Attract Inflows Amid High Valuations
